What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. The experience taught Grace more than any book could. At first, Grace found it difficult to keep the habit. The museum tells the stories of indentured laborers on the plantations.

There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Grace keeps a small bird at home and feeds it every morning. The bird-watching spot has become an important part of daily life. What's more, no feeder is truly squirrel-proof.

Kate advised Grace to try drawing as a new hobby. There are always more possibilities than we expect. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The hourly news bulletin repeats little.

People around Grace often share different ideas about the flower market. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. Kate always says that small steps matter more than big plans. The stumpery hosts ferns and fungi.
The flower market looked quieter than usual that evening. Grace is saving money to buy a ticket to Xi'an. Little by little, things began to change.
